title: Chapters 1–5 — check what stuck
intro: Ten self-check questions across the five chapters. These are my own checks against the lessons, not an official paper.

questions.prompt: Probing finds pin 1 ~ pin 4 and pin 4 ~ pin 9, but pin 1 ~ pin 9 was never closed. Which property fails?
choices: Reflexivity
Symmetry
Transitivity — and so the relation does not partition the board
None; it is still an equivalence relation
questions.explanation: Transitivity is the leg that fails in practice, because it asserts something about pairs nobody measured. Without it there is no partition, and the net list built from the data is wrong.

questions.prompt: A hydraulic ram clips at ±10°, so every stick angle past 5° gives exactly 10° of deflection. Why can't the original angle be reconstructed?
choices: The sensor resolution is too low
Injectivity is lost — the preimage of 10° is a set, not a value, so the information was never in the recording
The solver needs a better root-finding algorithm
The log rate is too slow
questions.explanation: Nothing is broken; the composite simply stops being one-to-one. No downstream cleverness recovers information that was never encoded — which is why the fix has to be upstream and structural.

questions.prompt: Why does cos⁻¹ use the branch [0, π] rather than [-π/2, π/2]?
choices: Convention inherited from tables
Because cosine rises then falls on [-π/2, π/2] — it isn't injective there, so no inverse can be defined
Because cosine is undefined on [-π/2, π/2]
To make it agree with sin⁻¹
questions.explanation: Every principal branch is chosen for one reason: strictly monotonic ⇒ injective ⇒ invertible. [0, π] is cosine's nearest monotonic (decreasing) window covering all of [-1, 1].

questions.prompt: Targets at (10, 10) and (-10, -10) both display a bearing of 45°. What went wrong?
choices: Floating-point error in the division
The arctangent library is inaccurate in the third quadrant
Forming y/x discarded both signs before tan⁻¹ ran, and the principal branch (-π/2, π/2) cannot represent a third-quadrant bearing anyway
The targets genuinely merged
questions.explanation: The information dies one step before the function everyone suspects. atan2(y, x) takes the two arguments separately, inspects both signs, and recovers the full (-π, π].

questions.prompt: tan⁻¹(1) + tan⁻¹(2) equals about 108.4°, but the sum formula returns about -71.6°. Why?
choices: The formula is simply wrong
Here xy = 2 > 1, outside the identity's valid regime; the formula's output is trapped in (-90°, 90°) so the regime correction of +180° applies
Degrees and radians were mixed up
tan⁻¹(2) is undefined
questions.explanation: The identity holds only for xy < 1. Beyond it you add π (both positive) or subtract π (both negative); at xy = 1 the denominator vanishes — the RF resonance condition.

questions.prompt: Why is 'are all the off-diagonal entries zero?' an inadequate structural check?
choices: It is too slow to compute
It cannot distinguish diagonal from scalar from identity — and those three make different physical claims
It fails for non-square matrices
It gives false positives on rotation matrices
questions.explanation: Identity ⊂ Scalar ⊂ Diagonal ⊂ Square. Diagonal means independent per-axis scaling; scalar means uniform gain kI; identity means untouched. Report the most specific class.

questions.prompt: A monitoring rig reports a large displacement-gradient tensor, but its symmetric part is near zero and the skew part carries the magnitude. What is happening?
choices: The structure is close to failure
The strain gauges have debonded
The section is rotating, not deforming — the skew half of A = P + Q is rigid-body rotation and does no damage
The tensor was computed incorrectly
questions.explanation: The decomposition A = ½(A + Aᵀ) + ½(A - Aᵀ) is unique, and it separates strain (symmetric) from rotation (skew). Only the symmetric half can damage anything.

questions.prompt: For AX = B with det A = 0, what distinguishes 'no solution' from 'infinitely many'?
choices: The size of the matrix
Whether (adj A)·B is non-zero (inconsistent — parallel lines) or zero (dependent — infinitely many)
Whether B is the zero vector
Nothing; det A = 0 always means no solution
questions.explanation: x + y = 3 with 2x + 2y = 7 versus the same pair ending in 6: identical coefficient matrices, opposite verdicts. The two demand opposite responses — add a constraint, or fix the contradicted input.

questions.prompt: |x| at x = 0 is the standard counter-example to which claim?
choices: That continuous functions are bounded
That continuity implies differentiability — |x| is continuous there, yet LHD = -1 ≠ RHD = +1
That differentiable functions are continuous
That limits always exist
questions.explanation: Differentiable ⇒ continuous holds; the converse fails. The corner is the obstruction, which is why ReLU needs a subgradient at the origin and why trajectories must be C² splines.

questions.prompt: For a parametric curve, why is d²y/dx² ≠ (d²y/dt²)/(d²x/dt²)?
choices: It is equal; both forms work
Because dy/dx is a function of t, so differentiating it with respect to x must chain again — dividing by dx/dt, not by d²x/dt²
Because second derivatives don't exist for parametric curves
Only when dx/dt = 0
questions.explanation: The tempting form drops the dt/dx factor. On x = a cos t, y = a sin t the truth is -(1/a)csc³t while the naive form collapses to tan t — at t = π/4 with a = 1, that is -2.83 against +1.00: wrong in sign as well as magnitude.
